corpusSummary: Across 2026 papers, researchers probe how large language models reshape social science inquiry, practice, and policy. The corpus reveals methodological use of LLMs as tools for data extraction, coding, and governance; investigations of user trust, representation, and dependency; health, education, and environmental applications; concerns about bias, safety, and ethical implementation; and the emergence of frameworks to ensure equity, transparency, and critical human oversight.

themes.name: LLMs as methodological instruments in social science
themes.description: A set of studies deploy LLMs for data extraction, coding, sentiment analysis, ethics review, and simulations, while calling for validation, transparency, and methodological rigor.

themes.name: Human–AI interaction, trust, and social dynamics
themes.description: Research examines trust, anthropomorphism, dependency, device embodiment, and persuasion across health, education, work, and everyday contexts.

themes.name: AI in health, wellbeing, and ethics
themes.description: Work on health misinformation, patient education, risk assessment, digital health equity, and culturally-aware governance of AI in health contexts.

themes.name: AI in education and learning systems
themes.description: Studies on AI-enabled tutoring, scaffolding, assessment, AI literacy, and impacts on student learning, instructor practice, and curriculum design.
